notes.title: Grounded 2: Survive the Rot and Ruin Update

items.text: Brookhollow Park is getting a little more rotten. The Rot and Ruin Update expands Grounded 2 with a new area to explore, dangerous creatures to face, another Buggy to saddle up on, and new ways to customize both your gear and your home away from home.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45651847/78c2769cda660a381454130c27af4d2e03bd1f28.png"]

A new adventure awaits in the Woodpile, where towering structures and winding passages have become home to a familiar threat. Termites are back, including Workers, Soldiers, the mighty Termite King, and new O.G.R.R. variants. But these aren't exactly the Termites you remember. Keep an eye out for new attacks and some particularly strange behavior as you make your way deeper into their territory.

And Termites aren't the biggest thing lurking among the rot. One of the community's most requested creatures is finally crawling into the Park. Prepare to face the Centipede, a formidable new boss with plenty of legs and even more reasons to run.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45651847/eb1729b56027555901ed6c0277f99cecf2c9afef.png"]

notes.title: Saddle Up on the Potato Beetle

items.text: Need some backup? The Potato Beetle Buggy is ready to roll. Bigger than the Ladybug Buggy and built for close-range combat, this Potato Beetle Buggy can unleash a spread of projectiles against creatures in front of it and use its Healing Roar to help keep you in the fight. It can also haul resources and contribute materials to blueprints while you're out building across the Park.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45651847/c0d7a7db7e0584cf8c2ba755f38fbb1228247878.png"]

Your base, your colors. Painting gives builders a new way to personalize their creations by crafting paint and putting it to use with a new paintball gun we are calling the Splotcher. Walls, floors, roofs, stairs, doors, and other structures can take on a fresh coat of color, giving you even more ways to make your corner of Brookhollow Park your own.

The Fall Update also introduces a new way to keep your favorite equipment growing alongside you. Weapons and armor can be upgraded to higher Tiers using Bismuth, a new resource connected to the strange forces of Raw Science beneath the Park. Gather it, refine it, and put it to work at the new Yoking Press to make your equipment even stronger.
And there's still more to discover, including new SCA.B Themes, collectible miniatures, new stations, and more when Rot and Ruin arrives in Grounded 2 this fall.

If you've spent time exploring Brookhollow Park, you've probably found yourself staring at the pond, wondering what was waiting beneath the surface.
[p align="start"]With Into the Abyss, it's finally time to take the plunge.

[p align="start"]Our biggest update yet expands the park with an entirely new underwater experience that transforms how you'll explore, build, and survive. From sprawling new locations and underwater base building to dangerous new creatures, expanded progression, and a new amphibious Buggy, this update isn't just about adding more space—it's about introducing a whole new dimension to Grounded 2.

[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-news-gnarly-bark.jpg" style="max-width: 100%; vertical-align: middle; border: 0px; height: auto !important; outline: none !important; box-sizing: inherit;"]
[p align="start"]The pond has always stood out as one of Brookhollow Park's largest landmarks, but what you've seen so far is only the beginning.

[p align="start"]Beneath the surface lies one of Grounded 2's largest new areas to date. What first appears to be a familiar pond quickly opens into a sprawling environment with surprising verticality, hidden routes, and new points of interest. Beyond the shoreline, you'll also venture into new surrounding areas, including the Bayou and the Mountains, while those willing to take the plunge can descend into the Abyss itself.

[p align="start"]Every dive rewards curiosity, but it also demands preparation. The deeper you descend, the more you'll rely on upgraded gear, careful planning, and your understanding of the environment to survive what waits below.

notes.title: Every Dive Starts Before You Enter the Water

items.text: [p align="start"]Surviving beneath the surface means preparing differently than you have before.

[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-news-toe-biter.jpg" style="max-width: 100%; vertical-align: middle; border: 0px; height: auto !important; outline: none !important; box-sizing: inherit;"]

[p align="start"]The new Diving Suit introduces a progression path built around underwater exploration. Discovering Optical Disks unlocks new Diving Suit recipes, allowing you to craft upgraded equipment for longer expeditions and opening access to even deeper parts of the pond.

[p align="start"]Rather than treating underwater exploration as a short detour, Into the Abyss makes it an entirely new gameplay loop. Each upgrade opens new opportunities to explore deeper, discover hidden resources, and uncover more of what the pond has to offer.

notes.title: Build a Home Below the Surface

items.text: [p align="start"]Players have built incredible creations throughout Brookhollow Park since Early Access began, and we're excited to see what you'll create next.

[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-news-underwater-base.jpg" style="max-width: 100%; vertical-align: middle; border: 0px; height: auto !important; outline: none !important; box-sizing: inherit;"]
[p align="start"]

[p align="start"]For the first time, you'll be able to establish fully underwater bases, opening entirely new possibilities for where and how you build. New underwater building pieces, including Bubble Floors that create breathable spaces beneath the surface, let you transform the depths into your next home, staging area, or research outpost.
[p align="start"]Whether you're building for function, creativity, or simply because you've always wanted an underwater base, this update expands your toolbox in exciting new ways.

notes.title: New Ways to Fight. New Reasons to Prepare.

items.text: [p align="start"]Of course, the pond isn't giving up its secrets without a fight.

[p align="start"]Into the Abyss introduces new underwater combat encounters with both familiar and brand-new creatures. Returning threats like the Diving Bell Spider now share the water with new predators including the Toe Biter, while CNK robots and Pond Jockeys create new dangers throughout the surrounding areas. Every expedition asks you to rethink your gear, builds, and approach before taking the plunge.

[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-news-toe-biter-buggy.jpg" style="max-width: 100%; vertical-align: middle; border: 0px; height: auto !important; outline: none !important; box-sizing: inherit;"]
[p align="start"]

[p align="start"]If you'd rather have a Toe Biter on your side than standing in your way, they can also be tamed and transformed into your newest Buggy. Its amphibious nature lets you seamlessly travel between land and water, opening new routes through the park while making exploration and combat feel more connected than ever.
[p align="start"]As always, choosing the right gear, mutations, and build before setting out can make all the difference once things go sideways.
[p align="start"]Beyond the pond itself, Into the Abyss expands Brookhollow Park with new collectibles, additional rewards for exploration, and more reasons than ever to wander off the beaten path.

[p align="start"]Hidden throughout Brookhollow Park are Critter Capz, collectible bug-themed figurines waiting to be discovered. Tucked away in hidden corners and off-the-beaten-path locations, they're a reward for curious explorers and completionists alike, encouraging you to revisit familiar areas and uncover every new path the update has to offer.

notes.title: Your Next Adventure Starts Below the Surface

items.text: [p align="start"]One of our goals with Grounded 2 has always been to make Brookhollow Park feel like a place worth exploring again and again.

[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-news-ziplines.jpg" style="max-width: 100%; vertical-align: middle; border: 0px; height: auto !important; outline: none !important; box-sizing: inherit;"]
[p align="start"]

[p align="start"]Into the Abyss takes that philosophy deeper than ever before. It's not just a new destination; it's a new way to experience the park. Every dive presents new choices, new dangers, and new discoveries waiting just below the surface.

[p align="start"]Whether you're chasing every collectible, building an underwater stronghold, or simply determined to see what lies at the very bottom of the pond, we can't wait to watch your next adventure unfold.
[p align="start"]Gear up, gather your friends, and take the plunge.
[p align="start"]We'll see you in Brookhollow Park.

Dive Into the Depths in Grounded 2's "Into the Abyss" Update
Grounded 2's "Into the Abyss" update launches August 11, opening the pond and one of the biggest new areas in Brookhollow Park
Explore above and below the water's surface with new progression systems, discoveries, and challenges waiting in the depths
Traverse land and water with the new amphibious Toe-biter Buggy while facing familiar and new threats throughout the pond
The pond is finally opening.
On August 11, Grounded 2's next major content update, Into the Abyss, arrives and brings players into one of the biggest new areas added to Brookhollow Park so far.
For the first time, players will be able to explore both above and below the water's surface, uncovering new locations, new challenges, and new mysteries hidden beneath the pond.
The deeper you go, the more there is to discover.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45651847/1e9ea87fced340c9c90a23f443f82aaf1e293725.jpg"]

Exploration plays a huge role in Into the Abyss. New diving suits help players stay underwater longer and reach deeper sections of the pond, opening up new paths and opportunities as they progress through the area. Into the Abyss is all about exploration. Players will journey through new areas like the Mountains, the Bayou, and the depths beneath the pond, each offering new discoveries and challenges along the way. New diving suits will help players stay underwater longer and reach deeper parts of the pond as they continue their adventure.
Of course, the water isn't empty.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45651847/1eaf3c54934bdba2d01d0379a6e195a1f97ce287.jpg"]
Creatures like the koi fish and diving bell spider make their return, while new threats wait beneath the surface for players brave enough to dive in.
Whether you're exploring solo or with friends, the pond is designed to make every trip into the depths feel like a brand new adventure.

Getting around the new area also comes with a new companion. The Toe-biter joins Grounded 2 as a new amphibious Buggy capable of traveling across both land and water, helping players explore more of the pond and tackle encounters in new ways.

For the team, Into the Abyss has been an opportunity to build on what players loved about underwater exploration in the original Grounded while applying everything we've learned since then. Community feedback helped shape our approach, and we're excited for players to finally get their hands on it.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45651847/cd03cb9b4b390a3f8a61eb2ff8b368188d75b61b.jpg"]
And while the pond is the star of this update, it's only one step in the journey. Brookhollow Park will continue to expand with new areas, creatures, systems, and surprises as development continues.
We can't wait to see what you find beneath the surface.

releases.displayName: Beat the Heat Update – Your Lizard Has Arrived

items.text: You asked for something bigger than bugs, and now it’s here.
The Beat the Heat update is now live in Grounded 2, bringing a new boss fight, a new buggy progression system, and a wave of content, improvements, and community-requested features across the park.
[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-bth-hoops.jpg"]
During your adventures out in the park you might find King Dozer, a massive horned lizard and one of the most dangerous creatures we’ve added yet.
This is a full boss encounter — one you’ll need to prepare for. You’ll summon it, face it head-on, and survive long enough to take it down.
[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-bth-gear.jpg"]

notes.title: If you do, the rewards speak for themselves

items.text: New weapons and armor crafted from its scales
Unique gear that reflects just how dangerous it is
Furniture and trophies to prove you took it down

notes.title: A New Way to Grow Your Buggies

items.text: This update brings a community-requested feature that we are excited to further develop alongside you, our community.
Buggy Progression is here and it introduces a full system for upgrading your buggies and making them a core part of your build.
Using Moldy Milk Molars, you can invest directly into your buggy’s growth:
Increase health, damage, and effectiveness
Improve how they gather and support you
Bring early buggies into tougher fights
You’ll also unlock mutations that reinforce each buggy’s role. Some are always active based on the creature, while others trigger from your actions, giving you more control in the park.
[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-bth-barrel.jpg"]
The Buffin’ Barrel lets you evolve your buggy to the next tier, increasing its power and what it can gather so it scales with you instead of falling behind.
And new additions like the Black Soldier Ant Buggy expand your options even further.
[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-bth-sinkhole.jpg"]
There’s more happening across Brookhollow Park than ever before.

A new point-of-interest landmark and anthill named the Sinkhole Anthill are appearing, along with new creatures, resources, and gear to chase down. You may also encounter O.G.R.R. creatures in the picnic and garden areas, adding new threats to familiar spaces.
[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-bth-ogrr.jpg"]

Building continues to expand with new sets and parts, plus utility structures like the Buggy Buff Hut and EverChar Roasting Spit, a new cooking device that can handle more food at once while keeping your base well lit.

notes.title: More Ways to Fight and Survive

items.text: Combat and survival continue to evolve.
You can now block while using a bow, adding more control to ranged fights. O.R.C. creatures have also picked up new abilities, including lasers and healing, making encounters less predictable.

notes.title: We’ve also made improvements across the board

items.text: Reworked poison gas and related gear
Smoother inventory navigation
Clearer bandage healing values in menus
[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-bth-easter.jpg"]
The Easter update is live alongside Beat the Heat.

Easter Eggs can now be found around the park, dropping marshmallows used in new Ranger Station recipes. Craft and eat s’mores for a sugar rush or build a Marshmallow Chair for your base when the recipe releases later this month (so stock up and start saving those marshmallows)!

notes.title: Make the Park Your Own with Playgrounds

items.text: Playgrounds Mode is ready, giving you the tools to shape the park your way. Create arenas, challenges, puzzles, or anything you can imagine, then share your creations with the community.
You can also dive into a growing collection of player-built worlds that are already live and waiting to be explored.

items.text: [p align="start"]Lead Community Scientist 347 and Field Intern 678 are here with a new mandatory update seminar for you to view as they discuss the new update.
Grounded 2 is in Early Access, and we’re continuing to build the game alongside the community. This update brings in some of your requested features, along with new challenges to take on.

Moldy Milk Molars

[p align="start"]New moldy molars for our buggies! Collect them and spend them to make your buggy stronger, just like regular molars for the teen. This will impact any buggy that follows you, now or in the future. Those moldy molar upgrades are tied to you as a player and are applied to any buggy that you summon, not to a particular buggy.
Buggy Max Health - Increases the maximum health of your buggy by an increment of 10%.
Buggy Max Stamina - Each upgrade adds a stamina chunk.
Healing - Any source of healing other than the natural health regen receives a buff for each upgrade with an increment of 20%
Health Pool on Revive - Increase the health pool of your buggy after you help it from the down state
Inventory Size - Increase the number of slots in your buggy inventory.
Mutations
[p align="start"]New Buggy Mutations! Just like the teen, your buggies can become better by performing certain actions.
Grass Master: Chopping power with Ant Buggies slightly increased.
Recruit Master: Your recruit(s) gain more health.
Rock Cracker: Busting power with ladybugs increased.
Block on Lock: The Ladybug Buggy's block reduces incoming attack damage.
Crit Machine: Crit chance slightly increased with a Spider Buggy's 3-hit combo.

Buggy Buffin'

[p align="start"]it is now possible to buff your buggies! This will upgrade any of your buggy to the next tier. This way, your Red Ant Soldier buggy will be able to keep up with you in your progression, or any other buggy for that matter.
[p align="start"]Buffin' a buggy means it has more health, does more damage and is able to gather resources from a higher tier (if able).

items.text: The garden is awake.

[dynamiclink href="https://youtu.be/hV5XHIaNN64"]Ominent’s experiments have taken a sour turn, and a strange new corruption is spreading across Brookhollow Park. Tang now stains the soil, seeps into water, and clings to unsuspecting creatures—and it’s up to you to survive whatever’s brewing beneath the surface.

Welcome to The Toxic Tangle, the first major content update for Grounded 2, available now for all players. This update expands the park with a new biome, new creatures, armor and weapons, trinkets, building sets, and a few threats that may be more than they appear.

Overgrown vines choke the greenhouse, creating twisting paths and hidden crawlspaces. These massive monstrosities and staggering structures all combine to produce that 'how do I get up there?' moment. The Garden biome is ripe for exploration, stacked with vertical climbs, secret stashes, and probably a bug or two you didn’t see coming.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45651847/c41ffd6c846f14ec96dfa9c7132654b410f51326.jpg"]

From the pumpkin patch to the carrot jungle, every corner offers something to harvest, hoard, or accidentally aggro. It’s big, it’s messy, and it’s absolutely crawling with trouble. Bring your best gear—and maybe a backup plan.
One of Grounded’s most iconic bugs is finally rideable—and she’s not here to play nice.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45651847/1ea8ed87338d3881319d8d91be806f12de77c3ef.jpg"]

The Ladybug Buggy is a heavy-duty, tank-style mount equipped with a pressurized water cannon. Use it to blast airborne pests out of the sky, rinse away sour Tang buildup, or just give your enemies a bad day. It can also ram headfirst into foes with a powerful charge and slowly regenerates health over time.
If you ever jumped on a ladybug in the first Grounded and wished you could stay there, this one’s for you.
The Garden is full of life, but not all of it wants to share the space.

New creatures like the coordinated Earwigs, the bulky Potato Beetles, and the soon-to-be fan-favorite, the Woolly Aphid, will challenge your reflexes, your timing, and your trust in anything with antennae.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45651847/c8fc6219be15eb236470902175f23e2c8cfa5273.jpg"]
You might also want to keep your eyes open. The Masked Stranger may have retreated after your first encounter, but she’s not gone—and she may not be alone.
Oh, and the Snake Colossus? You’ll know it when you see it. Probably right before it sees you.

Mutations have leveled up. They’re now split into active and passive types—actives still work the way you know and love, but passives now apply automatically based on your weapon loadout. That means less menu juggling and more time doing cool stuff, like perfect blocking a Tang-covered Rust Beetle or showing off your hybrid build mid-fight.

And for all the architects, decorators, and “I-just-need-one-more-wall-piece” players out there, this update’s for you. The builder toolkit gets a serious upgrade with new kits like the Pumpkin Set, a refreshed Mushroom Kit, Scale Roof Set, updated Acorn Stairs, and a community request for floor hatches. It's all about more pieces, better parity between sets, and smoother snapping to bring your backyard blueprints to life.

Whether you're crafting a greenhouse hideout, a pumpkin fortress, or a garden party palace, we can't wait to see what you build—and share. Tag us, drop it in Discord, or show it off wherever you hang out. We’ll be watching (with admiration, not binoculars).[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45651847/8636fa24804c24ce8b39d7b5f8e9d4ad6e9e14db.jpg"]
The Garden MIX.R and O.R.C. wave challenges are also live, ready for anyone who thinks they're tough enough to survive the swarm.
Lastly, the Founder’s Pack also grows with this update, adding new base-building items like the High Roller’s Dice Bag, Champion’s Banner, and more ways to personalize your park adventure.

Alongside this update, we’re preparing for the return of Playgrounds Mode, entering PTB (Public Test Beta) in February with all the core tools from the first Grounded. Whether you're building mini-games, boss arenas, or custom gauntlets, Playgrounds will give creators the tools they need to thrive. To keep an eye on what’s coming to Brookhollow Park, be sure to check out our updated roadmap for a sneak peek at what’s in store for Grounded 2.
There’s never been a better time to shrink down, suit up, and explore the weirdest corners of Brookhollow Park. The Toxic Tangle update for Grounded 2 is available now!
Ladybug Buggy

Eliminate your opponent with its anti-air cannon and be sure to clean the sky from any foes you meet along the way. With it, clean the Tang buildup you come across or decrease the Tang building on other friendlies....or enemies. Be sure to refill your reservoir at water sources around the park to never run out of ammo.

It's the most tanky and robust buggy yet, capable of healing itself and it has a slight resistance to the new tang effect spread across the Garden. Even with a cannon strapped to it's back that isn't its only mean of attack as the ladybug can unleash a powerful ramming maneuver that will knock your opponent out.
Tang
Ominent's latest experiments with sour resources have unsurprisingly... gone out of control, and now the garden is tainted with sour spills and caustic lakes.
Masked Stranger Boss fight

The Masked Stranger may have withdrawn from your first conflict with her; however she is far from defeated. Be on your toes as you could expect to see her again in the Garden and she may not be alone.
Snake Colossus
The unstoppable slithering serpent slinks savagely throughout the Croquet Court near the outside wall of the Garden. Prepare to meet our largest colossus yet!
New sap bandage
Now an easy way to heal your buggy!
Passive vs Active Mutations

Mutations are now split between active and passive. Active mutations will work like normal and still need to be equipped and swapped based on your situation. Passive mutations currently work with your weapon set and will be applied automatically when you switch equipment. There will be more passive mutations coming throughout development.

Come find out what's new with the Hairy and Scary Update!

[p align="start"]Brookhollow Park just got a whole lot creepier (and fuzzier). The Hairy and Scary Update has crawled its way into Grounded 2, and it’s bringing a monstrous new challenge, stylish new gear, smarter building tools, and even more ways to power up your Buggy. Ready to face your fears? Let’s dive in.
[p align="start"]
[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-axl-arena.jpg"]

[p align="start"]The park’s newest nightmare has eight legs, razor-sharp fangs, and enough hair to make your skin crawl. AXL, the tarantula boss, is here to put your courage to the test. Defeating this towering terror unlocks a full suite of tarantula-themed rewards:
Forge the imposing Tarantula Armor set
Wield the devastating Tarantula Bow and Spear
Add some spooky style to your base with chests, candles, and even a candlelit throne
[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-axl-gear.jpg"]
[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/grounded2-build-m.jpg"]

[p align="start"]Your grand designs just got easier. The new BUILD.M grid system makes snapping, placing, and perfecting your creations more intuitive than ever—so whether you’re raising a park empire or just tidying up your camp, your wildest blueprints can finally shine.
[img src="https://d1079ywfijtdjs.cloudfront.net/grounded2/gounded2-mantis-armor.jpg"]

[p align="start"]Exploring Brookhollow Park on wheels is smoother than ever. With Hot Pouch support fully integrated into your Buggy, you can scan, swap, and stock up without leaving the driver’s seat. Plus, a haunting new Praying Mantis armor set brings plague-doctor style and handy healing tricks to keep you rolling in one piece

[p align="start"]We’re thrilled to bring Japanese and Brazilian Portuguese localization to Grounded 2 in this update! More languages are on the way throughout development, so keep an eye on our socials and roadmap for what’s next

[p align="start"]Thank you all so much for your patience and support. Your feedback, suggestions, and bug reports have been invaluable with helping us build Grounded 2 together. If you continue to experience any further issues, please contact us at Obsidian Support.

issues.text: There are a few issues that will be present at the 0.2. These include the following:

A one-time regrow of all resources will be present on everyone's saves - we had reports of large base resources not regrowing, the fix for this is a result of everyone needing to chop down resources again under their base.

Players who left the PTB before it was finished will join the game with their Field of View (FOV) being set to 0 - to fix this please just change your FOV slider in the game options when you start up the 0.2 build for the first time and everything should return to normal.
